Asymptotic Variance–Covariance Matrix of the stationary distribution MLE

Source: R/03_stat.R
vcov_stat.Rd

Computes the asymptotic variance–covariance matrix of the maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) of the stationary distribution of an irreducible, finite-state Markov chain.

Usage

vcov_stat(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'MarkovChain'
vcov_stat(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'StochMat'
vcov_stat(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
vcov_stat(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A MarkovChain or StochMat object. Must be irreducible.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

Value

A numeric \(s \times s\) matrix, where \(s\) is the number of states, giving the asymptotic covariance matrix \(\Sigma_\pi\).

Details

Let \(P\) be the transition matrix of an irreducible finite-state Markov chain with stationary distribution \(\pi\). If \(\hat P\) is the MLE of \(P\) based on a long trajectory, then the induced estimator \(\hat\pi = \pi(\hat P)\) satisfies $$\sqrt{n}(\hat\pi - \pi) \xrightarrow{d} \mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma_\pi).$$

The implementation applies the matrix delta method using a Kronecker product: $$\Sigma_\pi = M\,\Gamma\,M^\top,$$ where \(\Gamma\) is the asymptotic covariance matrix for the row-wise vectorized transition estimator \(\mathrm{vec}(\hat P^\top)\) returned by vcov_p(). With \(\pi\) written as a row vector, $$M = \pi \otimes (I - P^\top + \mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^\top)^{-1}.$$

References

Gavrilopoulos, G., Trevezas, S., and Votsi, I. (2026). Matrix asymptotic calculus for plug-in maximum likelihood estimators in finite Markov chains. arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.17161. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17161. See Proposition 7 for the stationary differential and covariance.

See also

stat(), vcov_p(), is_irreducible()

Examples

P <- StochMat(matrix(c(0.8, 0.2, 0.3, 0.7), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))
Sigma <- vcov_stat(P)
dim(Sigma) # One stationary probability per state
#> [1] 2 2
